**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-06**
- **Member:** Emerson Delgado
- **Member ID:** W775387988
- **Reference number:** POC-17B712A980-60478
- **Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
- **Governing policy:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Joint Surgery — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), which PacificSource denied on 2026-08-06 on the grounds that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this surgery is needed, and I believe the records already in the plan's possession match the plan's own published criteria point for point. I am writing this appeal myself as the member.

Below I have set out the plan's own language from the Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Joint Surgery, and next to each one, what my medical records show.

## The plan's criteria and my records

**1. My shoulder problem came on gradually, without a recent injury.**

The policy describes, as a criterion:

> "Gradual onset of shoulder pain in the absence of a significant traumatic event within the preceding 3 months"

My records document 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not been relieved by rest. There is no traumatic injury in my history. The policy separately addresses the acute pathway with the criterion "Traumatic injury within the preceding 3 months with no preexisting shoulder pain (For traumatic injuries that occurred more than 3 months ago, see chronic or degenerative full thickness tear )" — which confirms that a gradual, non-traumatic presentation like mine is reviewed under the chronic or degenerative pathway, not the acute one.

**2. My symptoms have lasted well beyond the duration the policy requires.**

> "Symptoms are present for at least 3 months"

My symptoms have been present for 12 months and have been progressive throughout that time.

**3. My imaging confirms exactly the finding the policy names.**

> "Recent advanced imaging confirms features of a degenerative full thickness tear"

An MRI of the shoulder performed on 2026-05-29 shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy.

The policy also states:

> "Imaging report . The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months. In the absence of a detailed report, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

My MRI was obtained on 2026-05-29, which is within the past 12 months, and the report is detailed as to tear thickness, location, size and fatty atrophy grade. If the plan did not receive a complete copy of that report, I ask that it tell me so and I will arrange for it to be resent rather than have the request closed for a records gap.

**4. I completed conservative management, and more of it than the policy requires.**

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management"

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records show:

- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, 16 weeks, from 2026-02-17 to 2026-06-09, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Complementary strategies:** NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-07, which gave me only 3 weeks of partial relief.

That is 16 weeks of physical therapy — well past the 6 weeks the policy states — plus not one but two additional conservative treatments aimed at reducing inflammation and relieving pain. The policy further states:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

and

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My compliance is documented: 24 completed visits over 16 weeks, with a discharge note. I did the conservative care the plan asks for, in full, and my shoulder did not improve.

**5. My exam findings are consistent with a symptomatic tear.**

> "Physical exam consistent with symptomatic rotator cuff tear (e.g., drop arm test, painful arc, full/empty can test, weakness of internal/external rotation or abduction)"

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

**6. My pain interferes with my daily activities.**

> "Pain ≥ 3 on the VAS scale which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living"

I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side. My pain has been progressive over 12 months and is not relieved by rest, by four months of NSAIDs, or by a steroid injection that helped only partially and only for three weeks. If the plan requires a numeric VAS value recorded in the chart, my treating providers can supply it: [numeric VAS pain score as documented in the chart, to be supplied by the treating provider].

**7. The tobacco criterion is satisfied.**

> "For primary rotator cuff repair, adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco and nicotine products for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended."

My records document that I am a non-smoker. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.

## A request about the criteria applied

One of the plan's criteria statements available to me — "Rotator cuff repair is considered medically necessary for an acute full thickness tear when ALL the following criteria are met:" — ends in a colon and introduces a list of conditions that I have not been provided. I want to be clear that I am not reproducing or characterizing any part of the policy beyond the language quoted above. Because my presentation is gradual and non-traumatic, I do not believe the acute pathway is the applicable one; but if the plan applied that or any other specific criterion in reaching its decision, I ask that the plan identify, in writing, which criterion or criteria I was found not to meet and what evidence it considered.

## What I am asking for

I am asking PacificSource to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-06 (reference number POC-17B712A980-60478) and authorize the rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827, as recommended by Dr. Marchetti. In the alternative, I ask for a written explanation identifying the specific criterion I did not meet, and an opportunity to supply anything further that is needed. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with appropriate expertise in orthopedic shoulder surgery.

I understand that my appeal must be received by 2027-02-02, which is within 180 days of the date of the denial notice. I am submitting this letter, together with the Member Appeal Form and supporting documents, by [chosen method]. For the plan's records, the available submission channels stated by PacificSource are: electronically, by logging in to InTouch and selecting **Ask a Question** to send the form securely, or by email to **NewAppeal@PacificSource.com**; by fax to **541-225-3628**; by phone at **888-977-9299 (TTY 711)**; or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. PacificSource's own form notes that electronic submissions are processed more quickly.

Please contact me at the phone number or email above if anything further is needed. I would rather answer a question than have this decided on an incomplete file.

Thank you for your time and for a careful second look at this.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Delgado**
Member ID: W775387988
